Here's a description of the provided plot, following your guidelines:

The plot illustrates the relationship between temperature and accuracy for different methods. The x-axis is labeled “Temperature” with a linear scale ranging from 0.1 to 1.0, with tick labels at intervals of 0.1. The y-axis is labeled “Accuracy (Pass@8)” with a linear scale ranging from 62.5 to 80.0, with tick labels at intervals of 2.5. A brown line, marked with star-shaped markers, represents “On-policy RL” and begins at approximately 76.0 at a temperature of 0.1, rises to approximately 82.0 at a temperature of 0.7, declines to approximately 79.0 at a temperature of 0.8, and ends at approximately 80.0 at a temperature of 1.0. A red line, marked with star-shaped markers, represents “LUFFY” and begins at approximately 74.0 at a temperature of 0.1, rises to approximately 78.0 at a temperature of 0.5, declines to approximately 72.0 at a temperature of 0.6, and ends at approximately 74.0 at a temperature of 1.0. A gray line, marked with triangle-shaped markers, represents “SFT” and begins at approximately 75.0 at a temperature of 0.1, declines to approximately 71.0 at a temperature of 0.6, rises to approximately 74.0 at a temperature of 0.7, and ends at approximately 75.0 at a temperature of 1.0.
